source_name: Vestník verejného obstarávania (ÚVO) — official bulletin, notices index
why_relevant: Statutory publication channel under zákon 343/2015 Z.z.: every Slovak contract notice, award notice (oznámenie o výsledku VO), contract modification, cancellation and summary report must appear here. Highest-yield primary channel for banking/payments contracts (CPV 66xxx, 30144000/30233300, 72xxx).

source_name: ÚVO — Vyhľadávanie zákaziek (contract search with CPV filters)
why_relevant: The query interface over the bulletin corpus; supports CPV, authority, procedure-type and date filters — the operational entry point for building a CPV 66100000 / 66110000 / 66172000 / 30144000 / 30233300 / 72xxx watchlist.

source_name: Národný katalóg otvorených dát — Vestník VO daily XML datasets (ÚVO/NASES)
why_relevant: Each Vestník issue is published as an open-data XML dataset (e.g. 'Vestník 79/2026', 'Vestník 217/2025'), enabling deterministic, machine-readable ingestion of every notice including CPV codes, authority IDs, winners and awarded values — the ideal backbone for an automated A2 pipeline.

source_name: IS EVO / Elektronická platforma VO — EVO portal contract search
why_relevant: The mandatory electronic platform (povinné používanie od 1.2.2023) where the actual procurement procedure runs: tender documentation (súťažné podklady), Q&A, bid opening records. Gives technical requirement detail on POS terminals, ATMs, card issuing and processing far beyond the bulletin summary.

source_name: isepvo.sk — Elektronická platforma documentation & user manuals
why_relevant: Documents how IS EVO structures notices, document types and identifiers; the user manuals (manual_uchadzac.pdf, verejna_sutaz_vo.pdf) are effectively the schema reference for building a reliable collector against the platform.

source_name: ÚVO — Elektronické verejné obstarávanie (EVO) hub page
why_relevant: ÚVO's own map of which system carries which contract type (EVO vs EKS vs private certified systems). Essential to avoid systematically missing below-threshold banking/payments purchases that never hit the Vestník.

source_name: ÚVO — Spoločný slovník obstarávania (CPV) reference
why_relevant: Authoritative SK-language CPV code list; needed to fix the exact code set and Slovak labels used for banking, payment-processing, card and terminal categories in query construction.

source_name: UVOstat.sk — restructured ÚVO procurement data (results, CPV browse, buyer-supplier links)
why_relevant: Third-party rebuild of the ÚVO corpus with far better navigation: browse by CPV code, per-supplier and per-authority histories, links to CRZ contracts. Fastest way to reconstruct historical award share for banks/payment vendors in SK public sector.

source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ)
why_relevant: Contracts of state bodies and public institutions must be published here (§5a zák. 211/2000) and are only effective once published — so the signed banking/card/acquiring contract text, pricing annexes and terms appear here even when the procurement itself was below-threshold. Confirmed hits like 'Zmluva o vydaní a používaní platobnej karty' with Prima banka.

source_name: Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital — open data & API (CRZ, obchodný vestník, ÚVO-derived)
why_relevant: Provides REST/SQL APIs and SQL dumps over the central contract register and related registers since 2011, with ÚVO named among cited sources — the cheapest way to run bulk historical queries instead of scraping CRZ HTML.

source_name: Elektronický kontraktačný systém (EKS) / elektronické trhovisko — portal.eks.sk
why_relevant: Below-threshold and low-value contracts (zákazky s nízkou hodnotou) for commonly available goods/services are contracted here, typically via 72-hour auctions — captures small POS/terminal/card and banking-service purchases that never reach the Vestník. ~100k trades, >EUR 1bn cumulative.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (SK above-threshold notices) + TED API
why_relevant: Slovak above-threshold notices are mirrored to TED in structured eForms with stable CPV metadata and full multilingual fields; the documented TED API and bulk XML packages make it the most robust programmatic complement to the national Vestník for large banking/payments contracts.

source_name: OpenTender / Open Contracting Data Registry — Slovakia publication
why_relevant: Government Transparency Institute normalises SK national-portal plus TED data into OCDS across 35 jurisdictions, enabling cross-country benchmarking of banking/payments procurement volumes and supplier concentration — analytic layer, not a primary record.

source_name: verejnesutaze.sk — commercial tender monitoring portal (SK)
why_relevant: Commercial monitor with per-tender pages and CPV browsing; observed a concrete banking-sector item (SWIFT Credit Bureau services for EXIMBANKA SR), confirming it surfaces niche financial-services contracts. Useful as an alerting layer and cross-check on ÚVO indexing lag.

source_name: UCHADZAC.SK — Vestník VO monitoring/explainer service
why_relevant: Bidder-side service summarising and alerting on Vestník notices; secondary value as an alerting redundancy and as a plain-language guide to notice types (oznámenie o vyhlásení VO vs o výsledku VO) used in parsing rules.

source_name: ÚVO — Register verejných obstarávateľov / registre o hospodárskych subjektoch
why_relevant: Canonical identifiers for contracting authorities (and the economic-operator registers) — the join key that lets notices, CRZ contracts and company data be linked into one supplier/authority graph for banking and payments.

source_name: ÚVO — Evidencia referencií (performance references register)
why_relevant: Authorities record delivered-contract references for suppliers; reveals which vendors have actually executed banking/payments contracts and how the buyer rated them — a rare quality signal on incumbents that award notices do not carry.

source_name: Contracting-authority procurement profiles (e.g. MO SR, MH SR, MPSVR SR, indprop.gov.sk)
why_relevant: Each authority runs a 'profil verejného obstarávateľa' publishing its own contracts, orders and invoices — often earlier and with more annexes than the central bulletin, and covering low-value banking/payments purchases. Useful for targeted monitoring of the big spending ministries and state-owned entities.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (Supplement to the Official Journal of the EU) / SK: Dodatok k Úradnému vestníku EÚ
why_relevant: Legally mandated EU-wide publication channel for all above-threshold Slovak public contracts, including banking, payment, card-acquiring, cash-handling and core-banking IT procurements by Slovak public bodies, state banks (Eximbanka, SZRB), ministries and municipalities. Parallel to the national ÚVO Vestník but with structured eForms data, multilingual metadata and machine access.

source_name: TED Search API v3 (docs.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Documented, authentication-free read API over all TED notices; the primary machine-collection route for Slovak banking/payment tenders and award notices. Supports expert query language over eForms fields (buyer country, CPV, value, winner name).

source_name: TED bulk XML download (daily/monthly notice packages)
why_relevant: Full-archive bulk packages of TED notices in XML from 2011 onward (older archives via FTP), enabling historical baselining of Slovak banking/payment procurement volumes, incumbents and price levels rather than only forward-looking monitoring.

source_name: TED Open Data Service (data.ted.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Publications Office open-data front end for TED notices; complements the Search API for reuse-oriented datasets and SPARQL/linked-data style access to procurement notices including Slovak ones.

source_name: data.europa.eu — TED procurement notices dataset (Slovak locale view)
why_relevant: EU official open-data catalogue entry for TED notices, exposed in Slovak; useful as a stable catalogue pointer to distributions (CSV subset, XML) and licence terms for reuse.

source_name: TED eForms standard and eForms SDK
why_relevant: Defines the field/schema vocabulary (business terms, codelists, CPV usage) that Slovak notices are published in since Nov 2022. Essential to build reliable parsers and to know which fields (winner ID, framework agreement, estimated value) are actually machine-readable.
